PRESIDENT'S ORDER 7 OF 1991
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 7 OF 1991
HIGH COURT JUDGES (LEAVE, PENSION AND
PRIVILEGES) (AMEMDMENT) ORDER, 1991
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I,
1st October, 1991]
No.F. 2 (2)/91-Pub., dated 1-10-1991.--The following Order made by the President is
hereby published for general information:--
Whereas it is expedient further to amend the High Court Judges (Leave,
Pension and Privileges) Order, 1970 (P.O.No. 9 of 1970), for the purposes
hereinafter appearing;
And Whereas paragraph 2 of the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution
relating to the High Court provides that every Judge of the High Court shall be
entitled to such privileges and allowances, and to such rights in respect of
leave of absence and pension as may be determined by the President;
Now, Therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by aforesaid
paragraph, the President is pleased to make the following Order, namely:--
1. Short title and commencement.----(1) This Order may be called the High Court Judges (Leave, Pension and
Privileges) (Amendment) Order, 1991.
(2) It shall come into force at once.
2. Amendment of P.O. No. 9 of 1970:---In the High Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 1970
(P.O.No. 9 of 1970)
(a) in paragraph 5, in sub-paragraph (3), for the word "five"
the word "six" shall be substituted;
(b) after paragraph 7, the following new paragraph shall be inserted,
namely:---
"7-A. Encashment of leaves---A Judge who has, at the time of
retirement, three hundred and sixty-five days leave on full salary to his
credit, shall be paid six months's salary in lieu of leave not availed
of.";
(c) in paragraph 22-A, in sub-paragraph (2) for the words "two
thousand rupees", the word, "nine thousand rupees" shall be
substituted;
(d) in parahraph 22-B, in sub-paragraph (1), for the words, "three
hundred" the words "four hundred" shall be substituted; and
(e) after paragraph 22-C, the following new paragraph shall be inserted,
namely:--
"22-D. Facilities to retired Judges.--A Judge on retirement shall
be entitled at Government expense to the service of either a driver or an
orderly at his option. The services of a driver or an orderly, as the case may
be, will remain available, after the death of a Judge to his widow.
